event_text: World War I: In the culmination of the July Crisis, Austria-Hungary declares war on the Kingdom of Serbia and begins the Great War.
headline: Austria-Hungary Declares War on Serbia, July 28, 1914
story: Barry preened his feathers as he gazed out at the bustling streets of Vienna. 'Well, Susan, it's all come to a head. Austria-Hungary's just declared war on Serbia, and it's about to get messy.' Susan cocked her head to one side. 'The July Crisis, they're calling it. All started when Gavrilo Princip, a Serbian nationalist, assassinated Archduke Franz Ferdinand. Austria-Hungary's been itching for a fight, and now they've got their excuse.' Barry nodded. 'And with Germany backing them, it's not just a local squabble. Russia's already mobilizing in support of Serbia, and France is bound by treaty to Russia. It's a bit of a domino effect, really.' Susan ruffled her feathers. 'The complex system of alliances is about to get a thorough test, isn't it? Austria-Hungary's ultimatum to Serbia was always going to be a bit of a non-starter. Now it's just a matter of who joins in and when.' Barry took to the skies, circling back to his perch. 'The Great War, they'll call it later. For now, it's just a lot of posturing and saber-rattling. But it won't stay that way for long.'
regret_line: Austria-Hungary might regret not just talking things out over a nice cup of coffee.
winner_line: The war machine itself, which will churn out devastation and profit for years to come.
